class_id: a computation's 'I could not' sentinel is written to the database as if it were the answer
feature: any derive-then-persist path where the deriving function returns an in-band sentinel (0, -1, '', 'UNKNOWN', epoch) for missing or unparseable inputs, and the caller persists the return value unconditionally
symptom: a pure function returns a sentinel rather than throwing or returning undefined, because a sentinel is convenient for its OWN callers (comparisons, arithmetic, tests that pin it). The persisting caller does not distinguish sentinel from value and writes it straight through. The column now holds a value that means the opposite of what it says: not 'the quantity is zero' but 'nobody knows the quantity'. It is invisible to the usual guards — a 0 satisfies a non-negative constraint, a NOT NULL constraint and an optional-field schema; it is not a null, so null-coverage counts report the field as populated; and it sorts and aggregates as a real number, so averages and minimums are quietly wrong. The generic test is: for each source that writes a field, count how many of its rows hold the deriving function's sentinel. If ONE source accounts for all of them, the sentinel is leaking from that source's derive step rather than being a real observed value.
first_seen: 2026-09-20 — IPODhan `ipos.issue_size`, measured read-only on ipodhan_staging through the sanctioned tunnel while working item 14 (#728). 20 rows hold issue_size = 0. Partitioned by the writing source in `field_sources`, ALL 20 are BSE-sourced — 20 of 20, and no other source (CHITTORGARH 231 rows, ADMIN 31, NSE 14, MONEYCONTROL 11, DRHP 2) has ever written a zero. The mechanism: `computeBSEIssueSize` (scraper/src/scrapers/bse-api-scraper.ts) returns 0 when the share count or price floor is missing or unparseable, and `buildScrapedIPO` passed that return straight into `issueSize`. The sentinel is deliberate and its own unit tests pin it (`expect(computeBSEIssueSize(0, 120)).toBe(0)`), so the defect is not the function — it is the boundary where a scraped record is built. `issueSize` was ALREADY `.optional()` in the validator, so undefined was legal the whole time and no schema change was needed. Same measurement also found 17 non-zero BSE-sourced rows carrying the separate wrong-quantity defect #728 describes; the two are distinct classes sharing one source.
fix_prs: the guard: `issueSize: computeBSEIssueSize(shares, band.min) || undefined` at the single call site both BSE mappers share, so the sentinel stops at the persist boundary while the function keeps it for its other callers. Failing tests first (3 red: +0 received where undefined expected, on both the detail-only and list+detail mapper paths), then green, then mutation-checked by reverting the guard (2 failed). Writing the test also corrected a wrong assumption in the test itself: an unparseable PRICE BAND makes the mapper return null for the whole row, so only a missing SHARE COUNT reaches the sentinel path — pinned rather than left implicit. What the guard does NOT do: it does not repair the 20 existing zero rows, which need a source-backed repair, and 19 of the 20 have no completed document to re-derive from.
detection_check: none yet. The check that generalises: for every (field, source) pair, report the count of rows holding that field's sentinel value, and FAIL when one source accounts for effectively all of them — that is the leak signature and it fires on the second field to develop it. Cheaper and more specific than auditing each deriving function. Note what made this findable at all: `field_sources` records WHICH source wrote each field, so the population could be partitioned by writer. A table recording only the value could not have been decomposed this way, and the 20 zeros would read as 20 genuinely tiny issues.
